# FREQUENCY Systems

> A maritime operational intelligence company building the autonomous cargo execution layer for U.S. inland waterways.

FREQUENCY Systems is building a cargo-operations decision system for inland terminals. Initial focus is one terminal and one cargo-transfer workflow. The company is pre-pilot: no field performance, accuracy figure, crew reduction, timing comparison or terminal relationship is claimed.

## Status
- Stage: pre-pilot, proposed product behaviour
- Initial scope: one terminal, one cargo-transfer workflow
- Validation: a controlled six-phase simulation running configured scenario values, labelled illustrative
- Next demonstrable milestone: one cargo transfer run end to end against a terminal's real operating constraints

## The workflow
Observations -> operations record -> planning and resource allocation -> checks and operator approval -> execution interface -> outcome record.

An operator approves; the system proposes. Stale observations are shown as stale and not used until refreshed. Missing observations are reported, not interpolated. Conflicts and failed checks are raised for operator review.

## Vessel configuration (as supplied, illustrative scenario)
- BARGE-402, 45m x 10m
- Draft read at six fixed hull positions: FP, FS, MP, MS, AP, AS
- Mean draft, trim and list are calculated from those readings, not read directly
